plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp parent cycle for boxing with a build-focused emphasis on general strength, power, and enough conditioning to support the work. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main percentage-based lift before the main loading begins in Week 2. Because you only lift once per week, each session is full-body, keeps the highest-value work first, and uses controlled volume so it supports boxing practice instead of draining it.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body strength and simple explosive qualities while keeping conditioning supportive and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength work and keep power output sharp without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more of the work toward faster, sharper output while maintaining the strength you built.

exercises.name: 1. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on cleanly. Reset between reps and focus on fast takeoff and quiet landings.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use bodyweight only and reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Jump for height and stick the landing.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up in small jumps, then work up to one hard set with solid form. Stop at the first sign of form breakdown. This top set establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat this assessment later with more load at the same reps or the same load for more reps while keeping form solid.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if back squat setup is uncomfortable and keep the reps crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a hard set of 5 if barbell squatting is not yet stable.

exercises.name: 3a. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Drive the elbows back and pause briefly at the top. Use a load you can control cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a neutral or close grip and keep the torso steady.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Support the free hand and avoid twisting.

exercises.name: 3b. Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Use a steady lower, firm touch, and strong press. Leave 2 reps in reserve on each set.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if setup is comfortable and consistent.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Elevate the hands if needed to keep clean reps.

exercises.name: 4. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Keep the ribs down and hips tucked. Only roll out as far as you can control without the lower back dipping.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use small plates and keep the range controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Stability Ball Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the ab wheel is too demanding.

exercises.name: 5. Air Bike Intervals
exercises.notes: Build conditioning without wrecking the legs. Stay hard but controlled.

endurancePrescription.intensity: Around 8 out of 10 effort on the work bouts
